difficultyRationale: Platform-estimated: MODERATE — two directly linked geometry facts (inscribed-angle theorem, then area = ½ab sin C) applied in 2–3 routine steps; about 2–3 minutes.
stem:
In the given figure, $P$, $Q$, and $R$ are three points on a circle of radius 10 cm with $O$ as its center, $\overline{PQ} = \overline{RQ}$, and $\angle PQR = 45^\circ$. The figure is representative.
The area of the shaded region $PQRO$ is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ cm$^2$.

![Figure: A circle with centre O. Points P (lower left), Q (top) and R (lower right) lie on the circle. Chords QP and QR meet at Q with a 45° angle marked, and radii OP and OR join the centre to P and R. The shaded arrowhead-shaped region is bounded by Q–P, P–O, O–R and R–Q.](/pyq/2026/fig/Q10-1.png)

solution.quick: The inscribed angle $\angle PQR = 45^\circ$ gives the central angle $\angle POR = 90^\circ$. By symmetry $OQ$ bisects the shaded region into two congruent triangles with $\angle POQ = \angle QOR = 135^\circ$. Each has area $\tfrac12 \cdot 10 \cdot 10 \sin 135^\circ = 25\sqrt2$, so the total is $50\sqrt2$ cm², option **(C)**.

steps.title: Central angle from the inscribed angle
steps.body:
$\angle PQR = 45^\circ$ is an **inscribed angle** standing on arc $PR$ (the arc not containing $Q$). The angle this arc subtends at the centre is twice the inscribed angle:

$$\angle POR = 2 \times \angle PQR = 2 \times 45^\circ = 90^\circ.$$

So the (unshaded) triangle $POR$ is right-angled at $O$.

steps.title: Split the shaded region along OQ
steps.body:
The shaded region $PQRO$ is the quadrilateral with vertices $P \to Q \to R \to O$. It is concave at $O$ and shaped like an arrowhead. Draw the segment $OQ$, which lies inside the region and splits it into triangles $OPQ$ and $OQR$.

Because $PQ = RQ$ and $OP = OR$, both $Q$ and $O$ are equidistant from $P$ and $R$. So both lie on the perpendicular bisector of $PR$, and the figure is symmetric about line $OQ$. Hence $\triangle OPQ \cong \triangle OQR$ and

$$\angle OQP = \angle OQR = \tfrac{45^\circ}{2} = 22.5^\circ.$$

steps.title: Angles and area of triangle OPQ
steps.body:
In $\triangle OPQ$, $OP = OQ = 10$ cm (radii), so it is isosceles with base angles equal:

$$\angle OPQ = \angle OQP = 22.5^\circ, \qquad \angle POQ = 180^\circ - 2(22.5^\circ) = 135^\circ.$$

(Check: $\angle POQ + \angle QOR + \angle POR = 135^\circ + 135^\circ + 90^\circ = 360^\circ$ ✓.)

Using area $= \tfrac12 ab \sin C$ with the two radii and the angle between them:

$$[OPQ] = \tfrac12 \cdot 10 \cdot 10 \cdot \sin 135^\circ = 50 \cdot \frac{\sqrt2}{2} = 25\sqrt2 \text{ cm}^2.$$

steps.title: Total shaded area
steps.body:
$$[PQRO] = [OPQ] + [OQR] = 25\sqrt2 + 25\sqrt2 = 50\sqrt2 \approx 70.71 \text{ cm}^2.$$

**Cross-check (subtraction):** $[PQRO] = [PQR] - [POR]$. By the cosine rule in $\triangle OPQ$, $PQ^2 = 10^2 + 10^2 - 2\cdot 10\cdot 10 \cos 135^\circ = 200 + 100\sqrt2$. So

$$[PQR] = \tfrac12 \, PQ \cdot RQ \sin 45^\circ = \tfrac12 (200 + 100\sqrt2)\frac{\sqrt2}{2} = 50\sqrt2 + 50,$$

and $[POR] = \tfrac12 \cdot 10 \cdot 10 = 50$. The difference is $50\sqrt2$ ✓. A coordinate (shoelace) check in Python also gives $70.7107$.

The answer is option **(C)**.

solution.teaching:
Two circle-geometry facts do all the work here.

**1. Inscribed angle theorem.** Take an arc $PR$ of a circle with centre $O$. The angle it subtends at the centre, $\angle POR$, is **twice** the angle it subtends at any point $Q$ on the remaining part of the circle, $\angle PQR$. The reason is that $OP$, $OQ$ and $OR$ are all radii, so triangles $OPQ$ and $OQR$ are isosceles. Extend $QO$ beyond $O$. The exterior angle of $\triangle OPQ$ at $O$ equals $\angle OPQ + \angle OQP = 2\angle OQP$, and likewise the exterior angle of $\triangle OQR$ at $O$ is $2\angle OQR$. When $O$ lies inside $\angle PQR$, as here, these two exterior angles together make up $\angle POR$, so $\angle POR = 2(\angle OQP + \angle OQR) = 2\angle PQR$. A $45^\circ$ inscribed angle therefore means a $90^\circ$ central angle.

**2. Area of a triangle from two sides and the included angle:** $\text{Area} = \tfrac12 ab\sin C$. Whenever two sides are radii ($a = b = r$), this becomes $\tfrac12 r^2 \sin(\text{central angle})$, which is very handy in circle problems. Note that $\sin 135^\circ = \sin 45^\circ = \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$, since $\sin(180^\circ - \theta) = \sin\theta$.

**Handling an irregular shaded region:** split it into triangles whose sides are radii, or write it as a big triangle minus a small one. Always check the angles around the centre add up to $360^\circ$.

**In this question:** the "arrowhead" $PQRO$ splits along $OQ$ into two congruent triangles. Each has two radii of length $10$ meeting at $135^\circ$ (because $135 + 135 + 90 = 360$). The area is $2 \times \tfrac12 \cdot 100 \cdot \sin 135^\circ = 100 \cdot \tfrac{\sqrt2}{2} = 50\sqrt2$.

The quadrilateral diagonal formula gives a neat alternative: $\text{Area} = \tfrac12 d_1 d_2 \sin\varphi$ holds for any simple quadrilateral, including a concave one. The diagonals here are $OQ = 10$ and $PR = 10\sqrt2$ (the chord of a $90^\circ$ arc), and they are perpendicular. This gives $\tfrac12 \cdot 10 \cdot 10\sqrt2 = 50\sqrt2$ again.

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.explanation: $50$ is the area of the **unshaded** right triangle $POR$ ($\tfrac12 \cdot 10 \cdot 10$). It is not the shaded region.

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.explanation: $25\sqrt2$ is the area of only **one** of the two congruent triangles ($OPQ$ or $OQR$). The shaded region contains both.

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.explanation: $100$ would need each triangle $OPQ$, $OQR$ to have area $50$, i.e. $\angle POQ = 90^\circ$. In fact $\angle POQ = 135^\circ$, so each area is $25\sqrt2$.

solution.shortcut: The diagonals of $PQRO$ are $OQ = r = 10$ and $PR = r\sqrt2 = 10\sqrt2$ (since $\angle POR = 90^\circ$), and they are perpendicular by symmetry. So Area $= \tfrac12 \cdot 10 \cdot 10\sqrt2 = 50\sqrt2$.
solution.commonTrap: Forgetting to double the inscribed angle, i.e. taking $\angle POR = 45^\circ$. Another common slip is answering $50$ (the unshaded triangle $POR$) or $25\sqrt2$ (only half of the shaded region).

transcription.notes: Transcribed from the official paper rendering and independently checked against it. The stem (radius 10 cm, centre O, $\overline{PQ} = \overline{RQ}$, $\angle PQR = 45^\circ$, "The figure is representative.", area of the shaded region $PQRO$ in cm$^2$) and the options (A) 50, (B) $25\sqrt{2}$, (C) $50\sqrt{2}$, (D) 100 match the paper exactly. The figure (public/pyq/2026/fig/Q10-1.png) is the image embedded in the official PDF (page 7), identical to the diagram in the official crop; a faint GATE 2026 watermark is visible in its background. The segment OQ is not drawn in the official figure; the solution adds it as a construction line. Official crop Q10-2 shows only the next page's section header ("Q.11 – Q.35 Carry ONE mark Each") and contains no question content.

answerVerification.method: Blind independent re-solve + Python check agrees with official key
answerVerification.checkCode:
import math
r=10; d=math.radians
Q=(0,r); P=(r*math.cos(d(225)),r*math.sin(d(225))); R=(r*math.cos(d(315)),r*math.sin(d(315))); O=(0,0)
def ang(A,B,C):
    v=(A[0]-B[0],A[1]-B[1]); w=(C[0]-B[0],C[1]-B[1])
    return math.degrees(math.acos((v[0]*w[0]+v[1]*w[1])/math.hypot(*v)/math.hypot(*w)))
print(ang(P,Q,R), math.dist(P,Q), math.dist(R,Q))  # 45.0, PQ == RQ
pts=[P,Q,R,O]
area=abs(sum(pts[i][0]*pts[(i+1)%4][1]-pts[(i+1)%4][0]*pts[i][1] for i in range(4)))/2
print(area, 50*math.sqrt(2))  # 70.7106... both
answerVerification.notes: Blind hand derivation: the inscribed angle of 45° gives the central angle POR = 90°. With PQ = RQ, arcs PQ and QR are each (360° − 90°)/2 = 135°, so the region splits along OQ into two triangles with sides 10, 10 and included angle 135°, and the area is 2 × ½ × 100 × sin 135° = 50√2 ≈ 70.71 cm². Cross-checked as [PQR] − [POR] = (50 + 50√2) − 50, and with a coordinate shoelace computation (70.7107). This agrees with official key C.
